preconditions.expression: T == int(T) and T >= 1 and T <= 10**5
preconditions.description: T is an integer representing the number of test cases, where 1 ≤ T ≤ 10^5.

preconditions.expression: all(N == int(N) and M == int(M) and 2 <= N <= 2*10**5 and 0 <= M <= min(N*(N-1)//2, 3*10**5) for N, M in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and not line.startswith('1 ') and not line.startswith('2 ') and not line.startswith('3 ')))
preconditions.description: For each test case, N is the number of provinces (2 ≤ N ≤ 2*10^5) and M is the number of destroyed roads (0 ≤ M ≤ min(N*(N-1)/2, 3*10^5)).

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 2 and all(int(x) in range(1, N+1) for x in line.split()) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and line.startswith('1 ') or line.startswith('2 ') or line.startswith('3 '))
preconditions.description: Each destroyed road is represented by two distinct integers u and v (1 ≤ u, v ≤ N, u ≠ v) in the input.

preconditions.expression: all(u != v for u, v in (tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and line.startswith('1 ') or line.startswith('2 ') or line.startswith('3 ')))
preconditions.description: Each destroyed road connects two distinct provinces (u ≠ v).

postconditions.expression: stdout == '\n'.join(str(count_ways(N, M, destroyed_edges)) for N, M, destroyed_edges in parse_input(stdin)) + '\n'
postconditions.description: For each test case, stdout contains the number of valid ways to deploy Sena X and Sena Y, where the deployment satisfies all given constraints. The function `count_ways` computes this count based on N, M, and the set of destroyed edges.

postconditions.expression: all(count_ways(N, M, destroyed_edges) == int(count_ways(N, M, destroyed_edges)) and count_ways(N, M, destroyed_edges) >= 0 for N, M, destroyed_edges in parse_input(stdin))
postconditions.description: The output for each test case is a non-negative integer representing the number of valid deployments.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= count_ways(N, M, destroyed_edges) <= 2**N for N, M, destroyed_edges in parse_input(stdin))
postconditions.description: The count of valid deployments is bounded by 2^N (all possible subsets of provinces for Sena X).

postconditions.expression: all(any(subset and not subset == set(range(1, N+1)) for subset in valid_deployments(N, M, destroyed_edges)) for N, M, destroyed_edges in parse_input(stdin))
postconditions.description: There exists at least one valid deployment where Sena X is assigned to at least one province and Sena Y to at least one province.

postconditions.expression: all(all(not any(u in subset and v in subset for u, v in destroyed_edges) for subset in valid_deployments(N, M, destroyed_edges)) for N, M, destroyed_edges in parse_input(stdin))
postconditions.description: In every valid deployment, no two provinces connected by a destroyed road are both assigned to Sena X (since all roads not destroyed are bidirectional and must not have adjacent Sena X provinces).

postconditions.expression: all(all(all(v in neighbors(u) for v in range(1, N+1) if v not in subset) for u in subset) for subset in valid_deployments(N, M, destroyed_edges))
postconditions.description: For every province u in Sena X, all provinces not in Sena X (i.e., in Sena Y) must be adjacent to u in the original complete graph (i.e., not separated by a destroyed road).

postconditions.expression: all(all(not any(u in subset and v not in subset and (u, v) not in edges and (v, u) not in edges for u, v in destroyed_edges) for subset in valid_deployments(N, M, destroyed_edges)) for N, M, destroyed_edges in parse_input(stdin))
postconditions.description: For every province u in Sena X, all provinces v in Sena Y must be adjacent to u in the remaining graph (i.e., the road between u and v is not destroyed).
